description: Hey everybody! We are Deni and Neda, we are computer science students at RWTH Aachen. We love to apply our knowledge to something meaningful - and health monitoring for astronauts seems like just the thing! You are welcome to join our team, if you are also passionate about that. We would love it if you can bring some physics knowledge regarding the health risks for astronauts in space (not a must of course!)
summary:
HEALium is an integrated health monitoring and emergency assistance system designed to support astronauts during long-duration space missions, where limited medical resources and communication delays with Earth make autonomous healthcare essential.

Our platform combines continuous health monitoring, daily physical and mental health assessments, environmental exposure tracking, and personalized health recommendations. By comparing current measurements with individual health baselines, HEALium identifies unusual changes and helps astronauts understand how their health may affect upcoming mission tasks.

In emergencies, HEALium provides an intuitive interface for reporting symptoms, identifying affected body areas, and accessing step-by-step medical guidance using available onboard equipment. Relevant health information is also shared with the flight surgeon to support remote medical assessment.

HEALium aims to improve astronaut autonomy, reduce the cognitive burden of health management, and support safer decision-making in isolated space environments. By bringing preventive monitoring and emergency assistance into one accessible platform, our solution addresses a critical challenge of future Moon and Mars exploration.
details:
The Problem

During long-duration space missions, astronauts face health risks such as radiation exposure, sleep disruption, bone loss, fatigue, and psychological stress.

Medical emergencies become especially challenging when no doctor is onboard, medical equipment is limited, and communication with Earth is delayed.

How can astronauts receive meaningful medical guidance when immediate professional assistance is unavailable?

Our Solution: HEALium

We developed HEALium, an integrated health monitoring and emergency guidance prototype that combines personal health information, wearable measurements, and symptom reports to support autonomous medical decision-making.

The platform consists of two main components.

1. Emergency Guidance

HEALium helps crew members respond to medical situations through a structured, intuitive interface.

When an emergency is reported, nearby crew members can be alerted. The assisting astronaut can identify the type of emergency, select affected body areas on an interactive human model, and describe the symptoms.

HEALium then presents possible causes and relevant next steps based on the information available in the demonstration scenario.

For example, our prototype demonstrates an astronaut experiencing severe lower-back pain. The system considers simulated historical measurements, including increased urinary calcium, reduced fluid intake, and bone loss, when presenting kidney stones as a possible explanation.

The assisting crew member can access illustrated, step-by-step instructions for relevant onboard medical examinations and procedures.

The system is designed to support non-medically trained crew members while keeping the flight surgeon involved when communication is available.

2. Preventive Health Monitoring

HEALium also supports astronauts in their everyday health management.

Its personalized dashboard brings together:

  • Wearable measurements, including heart rate, sleep, and activity.
  • Daily physical and mental health assessments.
  • Historical medical and laboratory information.
  • Environmental monitoring.
  • Personal baseline comparisons.
  • Scheduled health checks and reminders.
  • Mission-task recommendations.

Rather than comparing every measurement against a generic population average, the platform emphasises changes relative to an astronaut's individual baseline.

It also connects health observations with upcoming activities. For example, reduced sleep and slower reaction time may indicate that a demanding task requires additional review.

Recommendations are presented with explanations and caution indicators rather than unsupported medical risk percentages.

How It Works

HEALium organizes three main information sources:

Medical records: Health history, relevant laboratory results, and medication information.

Wearables and sensors: Heart rate, oxygen saturation, sleep, activity, and other available measurements.

Personal input: Symptoms, pain location, daily assessments, and descriptions of events.

The prototype uses this information to present understandable health summaries, possible explanations, and suggested next steps.

Its user interface prioritizes clear instructions, reduced cognitive workload, and accessible interaction during stressful situations.

Innovation and Impact

HEALium's main innovation is integrating preventive health monitoring, symptom assessment, medical guidance, and mission-task planning into one platform.

It is designed not only for doctors but also for astronauts who may have limited medical training.

The same approach has potential applications beyond space, including maritime operations, polar research stations, offshore facilities, and remote communities.

Our vision is to make medical guidance more accessible wherever immediate professional care is difficult to obtain.

Development and Limitations

HEALium was developed during the NASA Space Apps Challenge 2026 as an interactive software prototype.

The team combined user-interface design, interactive medical workflows, health-data visualization, and AI-assisted development.

Demonstration scenarios use simulated medical and environmental data where real astronaut measurements are unavailable.

HEALium is not a certified medical device. Its possible-cause suggestions, medical instructions, and task recommendations require professional validation before real-world use.

Future development could integrate authenticated onboard medical devices, validated clinical guidance, secure health records, and reliable communication with medical professionals.

Our vision: Medical expertise for every human, wherever they are.
